name: Haas delay + per-channel phase offset width, automated, with mono check
goal: Widen a mono synth or pad without panning by combining a small inter-channel delay (Haas range, kept under ~20 ms and often below 15 ms) with a filter-based phase offset on one channel (more mono compatible because it only shifts some frequencies), then automate the width on and off for drops/sections and always confirm in mono that comb filtering is acceptable.

source.title: Principles of Mixing 38 - Stereo Widening with Haas Effect and Phase

prerequisites: Stereo tool or delay with independent L/R delay offset; all-pass/phase-offset per channel (any 'stereo shaper' style plugin or Web Audio DelayNode + BiquadFilter allpass); mono-sum monitoring

inputs.name: delay_ms
inputs.description: Inter-channel delay, ≤20 ms (≤15 ms if audible on the source)

inputs.name: phase_offset
inputs.description: Amount of all-pass phase shift on one channel

outputs.name: widened_stereo
outputs.description: Wider image that leaves center elements (kick/snare) clear, with acceptable mono sum

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.
Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with the plugin/hardware vendors named in the source video; recreate with comparable modules.
Portable alias: Haas = short L/R delay offset; phase offset = all-pass filter on one side.

Delta vs pad-width-no-phase-smear-highband-pan-or-chord-split and unison-odd-even-detune-width-clean-supersaw: time/phase-difference widening with automation and a mono check, not band panning, split chords, or unison.

steps.action: Start with the mono source through a stereo tool set to pass-through; confirm it is centered.
Add a delay between left and right. Large offsets are heard as an echo; stay in Haas range (≤ ~20 ms, and for some sounds even 15 ms is noticeable) so it reads as width/position instead.
steps.expect: Image moves/widens without an audible slap

steps.action: Sum to mono: time offsets cause comb filtering (static phaser-like coloration). Reduce the delay or skip the effect if the mono sum sounds hollow or wrong.
Add phase offset (filter-based phase shift) to one channel instead of, or with, the delay; it only moves some frequencies so it is more mono compatible.
Combine a small phase shift with a small delay shift (try either direction) to place the sound wide and out of the way of centered kick/snare; as an alternative to panning it stays on both sides.
steps.expect: Element sits wide while center stays clear

steps.action: Automate the widener: off for verses, on (or wider) when a drop hits, or sweep from wide to mono for contrast.
steps.expect: Space audibly opens at the section change

steps.action: Before rendering, do a final mono check of the full mix.
steps.expect: No collapsed or phasey elements in mono

verification: Mono sum checked and comb filtering judged acceptable
Width automation changes the image at the intended section
